newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Ceausescu son's body flown home for burial.
newsitem.headline: Ceausescu son's body flown home for burial.

text.p: The body of Nicu Ceausescu, a son of Romania's late communist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu, was flown home on Friday for burial near the graves of his parents.
Friends and relatives chartered a plane to fly the body to Bucharest after Nicu, 45, a hard-drinking playboy, died in a Vienna hospital on Thursday from an acute liver disease.
Several cars carrying the Ceausescu family followed the funeral van which took his coffin across Bucharest to a chapel in the Ghencea cemetery where his parents are buried.
Nicolae Ceausescu and his wife, Elena, were shot by firing squad during the anti-communist revolt in December 1989 which ended their ruthless 24-year rule.
Nicu's brother Valentin and sister Zoe were visibly moved during a brief religious ceremony perfomed by an Orthodox priest as Nicu was laid in state in the chapel.
Nicu, who had been groomed to succeed his father, was arrested during the 1989 revolution and charged with ordering troops to fire on anti-communist protesters in the Transylvanian city of Sibiu.

He denied the charge, insisting he had left the city before troops shot dead 91 people and wounded about 200. He was jailed in September 1990 for 20 years but released on health grounds in November 1992.
